layer1.name: TrailBill
layer1.description: Invoicing and deposit collection for solo hiking guides. Included because of how its evidence is distributed: fifteen conversations logged against the assumption that was cheapest to test, and none against the one that could kill the idea.
layer1.outcome_note: Synthetic fixture. Not a real company and not counted toward separation statistics.

layer2.pins: THE GAMING VECTOR, as an end-to-end regression test. Fifteen primary conversations sit against an impact-1 assumption and zero against the impact-5 one. Evidence Quality must stay near 17, not near 100 — coverage is impact-weighted, so testing the cheap thing thoroughly buys almost nothing. If a future change makes Evidence Quality a claim count or a plain ratio, this entry's score jumps and the cap becomes purchasable with busywork. That is the single most valuable thing in this directory to keep passing.

assumptions.statement: At least 5 in 10 independent hiking guides running 20 or more trips a year have lost more than $500 to unpaid deposits in the past season

falsification_criterion.applies_to: independent hiking guides running 20 or more trips a year
falsification_criterion.observation: ask them to total their unpaid deposits from last season

assumptions.statement: At least 8 in 10 independent hiking guides already send invoices from a phone rather than a laptop

falsification_criterion.observation: ask which device they used to send their last invoice
